public_rationale: Reuters reported in March 2026 that OpenAI offered private equity firms preferred stakes with seniority and downside protection, under a section headed 'sweeteners'. In May 2026 the joint venture reportedly closed with a 17.5% guaranteed annual return. Reports on Amazon's $50B commitment say $35B depends on an IPO or an AGI milestone. These match the concessions Marcus named, and Reuters describes the private equity terms as better than what Anthropic offered. 'More and more' is loose wording, and I found no strict round-by-round comparison. Even so, the plain reading holds: in the months before the post, OpenAI was agreeing to unusual investor-friendly terms.
limitations: The terms come from anonymous-source reporting, not public contracts.
The 17.5% guarantee applies to a joint venture, not to OpenAI's main equity round.
The trend part of 'more and more' was not measured against earlier rounds.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: in its recent fundraising, OpenAI has been agreeing to terms that favor investors (contingent tranches, guaranteed returns, seniority, downside protection) beyond ordinary equity terms.
No period was named. I read it as describing OpenAI's 2026 fundraising up to the post date (January 2026 to 2026-06-10), which covers the deals he mentions.
'More and more' is read loosely: a run of new, unusually investor-friendly terms in recent deals. A strict measured increase compared with every earlier round is not required.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports from early-to-mid 2026 show OpenAI giving investors unusual protective or sweetened terms, such as contingent tranches or guaranteed minimum returns.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reports show that OpenAI's recent deals used plain equity terms without special investor protections, or that the reported sweeteners never existed or were withdrawn.
